clarification: Agent means a human real estate professional in this contract, not an AI agent or automation principal.
human_quotes: I’m talking about other real estate agents not AI agents
Like Carr has 150+ real estate agents. Some are teams like me and Dell. Some are single agents.
one_sentence_gap: CARR has more than 150 human real estate agents, including solo agents and multi-agent teams, and needs to license them without a company-tenant seat becoming access to Joe and Dell's Panhandle business workspace or any other agent's book.
candidate_locations: search, files, calls, AI memory, integrations, and offline projections
sharing, referral, transfer, revocation, and audit
crux: The problem appears only if CARR tenant membership is treated as a tenant-wide data role. A human seat should establish identity and licensing; business-data access should come from separate, explicit workspace memberships.
recommendation: Use one CARR company tenant designed to support more than 150 licensed human users through multiple isolated business workspaces. Joe and Dell belong to the Panhandle Team workspace. Each solo real estate agent receives an individual CARR seat plus a private agent workspace. Each real estate team receives a team workspace whose members are explicitly assigned. A new seat has zero business-workspace access until membership is granted, and no seat receives tenant-wide search or data visibility by default.

scale_and_rollout.known_company_shape: CARR has more than 150 human real estate agents; some are solo agents and some operate in multi-agent teams.
scale_and_rollout.phase0_design_target: Pre-engineer the tenant, workspace, human-membership, resource-visibility, search, sharing, revocation, audit, and projection rails now, while they are inexpensive to establish, so later scale does not require redesigning the authorization or data model.
scale_and_rollout.launch_scope: The only planned operating workspace remains Panhandle Team with Joe and Dell. The architecture must be capable of later supporting CARR's 150-plus users, but this proposal does not plan or authorize onboarding them.
scale_and_rollout.commercial_scope: This is scalability preparation, not a commercial-launch plan. It does not authorize public SaaS, public signup, billing, self-service tenant creation, a client portal, company-wide rollout, or even a decision to offer the product to other CARR agents. Any later rollout is a separate evidence-gated business and product decision.

hierarchy.purpose: Joe-owned software, identity, policy, release, and licensing control
company boundary for more than 150 verified human identities, licensed seats, approved corporate-shared resources, and tenant policy
primary data and operating isolation boundary inside the tenant
record-level visibility no broader than the owning workspace unless intentionally promoted or shared

seat_contract.seat_effect: A seat permits one verified human to authenticate to the CARR tenant and use licensed modules. It grants no business workspace, record, search, file, call, memory, integration, export, or offline-pack access by itself.
seat_contract.solo_agent_default: Create one private business workspace owned by that human after approved provisioning.
seat_contract.team_agent_default: Join only the explicitly approved team workspace or workspaces. Team membership never implies access to Panhandle Team or another team.
seat_contract.multi_workspace_rule: A human may hold explicit memberships in more than one workspace, but every request and screen is bound to one server-derived active workspace context. Cross-workspace search and aggregation are denied unless a separately approved corporate view defines exact fields and purposes.
seat_contract.seat_removal: Disabling a seat revokes sessions and workspace memberships; business records remain with their owning workspace under the approved ownership and retention policy. Any transfer is a separate reviewed workflow.

workspace_roles.workspace_owner: Controls membership and ordinary workflow configuration inside one workspace but cannot change platform policy, tenant security, another workspace, or source code.
workspace_roles.workspace_member: Reads and writes only the records and modules allowed by role inside explicitly assigned workspaces.
workspace_roles.tenant_seat_admin: Provisions or disables human seats and approved modules but has no automatic business-record, search, file, call, memory, integration, export, or offline-pack access.
workspace_roles.tenant_compliance_reviewer: Receives only a separately defined, logged, purpose-bound view or time-limited case access; tenant administration alone does not confer this role.
workspace_roles.platform_owner: Joe controls platform, IP, release, security policy, tenant provisioning, and licensing; platform control does not silently read tenant business payloads.

server_derived_context.derivation: The server derives tenant and active workspace from the authenticated human, current membership, route, and approved context switch. Browser, URL, model, Doc, Hermes, job, record reference, and request payload cannot select a workspace or visibility class as authority.
server_derived_context.authorization: effective_access = intersection(active seat, tenant, exact active workspace membership, workspace role, module entitlement, resource visibility, record or field policy, purpose or workflow, environment, session freshness, and revocation state)
server_derived_context.default: deny before existence or metadata disclosure

not_inherited_by: Doc or Hermes operating for another workspace
protected_surfaces: clients, leads, deals, contacts, activities, and events
calls, audio, transcripts, notes, and summaries
email, calendar, provider, and other integrations
exports, reports, backups, and offline packs
Workspace, Control Room, Doc, Hermes, and local-edge projections
panhandle_isolation.search_rule: Every search and embedding result is workspace-filtered before ranking, snippets, counts, facets, or existence signals are produced.
panhandle_isolation.integration_rule: Credentials, mailboxes, calendars, storage mounts, and automation queues are owned by one user or workspace and are never tenant-shared merely because the connector is installed once.
panhandle_isolation.ai_rule: Doc or Hermes receives the active human and workspace context from the server. Its conversation, retrieval, memory, tool results, and scheduled work cannot cross workspace boundaries or merge tenant-wide context.

sharing_and_corporate_views.explicit_share: Cross-workspace collaboration uses a typed share or referral object naming sender, recipient workspace, exact fields, purpose, expiry, revocation, and provenance. It does not grant access to the source workspace.
sharing_and_corporate_views.corporate_shared: Only deliberately promoted templates, policies, vendor-directory entries, market resources, or similarly approved records enter corporate-shared scope; no Panhandle client or deal data is promoted by default.
sharing_and_corporate_views.corporate_reporting: Any firm-level reporting uses purpose-built minimum-field projections, explicit lawful purpose, and aggregation thresholds. Raw team books and tenant-wide search are not the reporting substrate.
sharing_and_corporate_views.no_global_switch: There is no tenant selector or 'view all teams' capability for ordinary users. Any future firm-wide supervisory capability is separately approved, narrowly fielded, audited, and never implied by an admin title.

single_agent_and_team_rules: A solo real estate agent is a human user with one private workspace; no team object is required.
A real estate team is a workspace plus explicit human memberships and workspace roles, not a shared login.
Every human keeps an individual identity, session, attribution, personal preferences, and personal-brain scope even when working in a team workspace.
Adding a member changes only that workspace's membership; it does not expose other workspaces owned by any team member.
One human's membership in two teams does not create a bridge between the teams; records move only through explicit share or transfer workflows.
Leaving a team revokes that membership and cached/offline access without deleting the workspace's canonical history.
required_denials: new valid CARR seat attempts Panhandle record or route before any workspace membership
solo agent requests Panhandle client, deal, search, attachment, call, memory, queue, integration, audit, export, or offline pack
member of another team guesses a valid Panhandle record identifier
tenant seat administrator attempts business-data access without separate workspace or compliance grant
user changes workspace_id, team, visibility, or tenant in URL, browser storage, model prompt, Doc request, Hermes request, or API payload
cross-workspace search leaks count, facet, snippet, embedding, existence, or autocomplete information
corporate-shared view includes an unpromoted Panhandle record
removed or expired member resumes a cached cursor, background job, export, attachment URL, or offline pack
acceptance_tests: A newly provisioned human seat authenticates successfully but sees no business records, search results, files, calls, memory, integrations, or workspace navigation until membership is granted.
Joe and Dell can operate Panhandle Team while another valid CARR human receives privacy-safe not-found parity across every protected surface.
A solo agent can operate a private workspace without a team object or visibility into another workspace.
A team member sees only explicitly assigned team workspaces and retains individual attribution.
Tenant seat administration provisions and disables users without acquiring business-data access.
Explicit share exposes only the approved fields to the recipient workspace and revocation removes future access without rewriting source history.
Cross-workspace search, Doc, Hermes, queues, integrations, reports, exports, and offline packs enforce the same workspace boundary.
Membership removal or seat disablement invalidates sessions, cursors, jobs, signed URLs, local cache, and offline data within the stated revocation SLO.
Audit reconstructs human, tenant, active workspace, membership, role, purpose, result, share or supervisory grant, and evidence without exposing unrelated workspace payloads.
council_question: For CARR's 150-plus human real estate agents, adopt workspace membership—not company-tenant seat—as the business-data authorization boundary for solo agents and teams?
proposed_council_language: Pre-engineer one CARR company-tenant architecture capable of supporting more than 150 human real estate users through separately isolated business workspaces, while planning to operate only Panhandle Team with Joe and Dell. A future solo agent could receive an individual human seat and private workspace; a future real estate team could receive a workspace with explicit individual memberships. A seat grants authentication and licensed modules but zero business-data access by itself. Search, files, calls, AI memory, queues, integrations, audit, exports, offline packs, Workspace, Control Room, Doc, Hermes, and local-edge views are workspace-scoped. Tenant administration does not imply business-data access, and cross-workspace collaboration uses typed, minimum-field shares rather than broad visibility. This is cheap structural preparation, not approval for commercialization, public SaaS, signup, billing, or onboarding any additional CARR users.
